_about.use_case: UC6 - Flood Warning System (Environment Agency to Leidos)
_about.description: Matches Environment Agency flood-risk-area postcodes against EE mobile customer addresses to identify the MSISDNs to warn, replacing a ten-year-old Ab Initio ETL. Six bronze streaming tables (named after their source feeds), one COUNT(*) presence gate, five silver/gold materialized views carrying the business rules, four pgp_zip exports. Design: BT_Usecase/UC6/docs/BUILD_CONTRACT.md; deviations with evidence: BT_Usecase/UC6/docs/FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_MAP.md; every attribute explained: BT_Usecase/UC6/docs/UC6_MASTER_DOCUMENT.md section 13.

ingestion_flows.source_description: UC6: the Environment Agency's weekly flood-risk address request (PAF-shaped, 14 pipe-delimited fields WITH a header row). Delivered gzip-then-GPG-symmetric (AES256); the framework decrypts the envelope using the br_digital_poc.config.pgpkey UC secret and decompresses the gzip member before Auto Loader reads it, all inside one pipeline update.

rules.expression: targetAreaID IS NOT NULL AND length(trim(targetAreaID)) > 0
osapr IS NOT NULL AND length(trim(osapr)) > 0

ingestion_flows.source_description: UC6: CSS account address records (PAYM/OUK). 19 pipe-delimited fields, headerless. Joined to CSS Account on customerid and normalised into the common PAF shape.
UC6: CSS subscription records (PAYM/OUK) carrying the MSISDN. 47 pipe-delimited fields, headerless. The driving side of the CSS three-way join.

UC6: CSS account records (PAYM/OUK) carrying dateofbirth and customerbusinessunitcode -- the two documented business filters (age > 17, unit code != 'BS'). 56 pipe-delimited fields, headerless. NOTE the file_pattern is CSS_account_[0-9]*, not CSS_account_*: the latter ALSO matches CSS_account_address_*, whose 19-field schema would corrupt this 56-field table.
UC6: JT Customer Details (PAYG/OUK). 34 pipe-delimited fields, headerless, carrying address and MSISDN inline -- there is no separate address feed for this channel.

UC6: Excalibur address records (EE/TMUK). 43 COMMA-delimited fields, headerless -- the supplied brief states pipe for every source, but this feed contains no pipes at all (see docs/UC6/FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_MAP.md section 3.1). Two record variants place the address in fields 18-20 or 19-22; both are handled in the PAF normalisation SQL.

transformation_flows.transformation_sql: SELECT 'ea_request' AS source_name, count(*) AS row_count FROM gate_ea_request UNION ALL SELECT 'css_account', count(*) FROM gate_css_account UNION ALL SELECT 'css_account_address', count(*) FROM gate_css_account_address UNION ALL SELECT 'css_subscription', count(*) FROM gate_css_subscription UNION ALL SELECT 'jt_customer', count(*) FROM gate_jt_customer UNION ALL SELECT 'excalibur_address', count(*) FROM gate_excalibur_address
transformation_flows.source_description: UC6 presence gate: one row per required source with its bronze row count. The single row_count > 0 expectation (action fail) is what fails the update when a weekly file is missing or empty -- a per-row dq_config rule on the ingestion flow cannot fire on zero rows. Every count is a groupBy-less aggregate, so each row exists even over an empty table. The three flows that read bronze directly CROSS JOIN this gate, so the failure lands before any silver/gold materialized view is recomputed to nothing. Replaces the six pipeline_audit_only self-reconciliation flows on 2026-09-08.

transformation_flows.transformation_sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT targetAreaID, trim(osapr) AS osapr, postcode, town,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY trim(osapr) ORDER BY __framework_ingestion_timestamp_utc DESC) AS rn
  FROM ea_request_for_base
  WHERE osapr IS NOT NULL AND trim(osapr) <> ''
)
SELECT targetAreaID, osapr, postcode, town
FROM ranked
CROSS JOIN (SELECT count(*) AS present_sources FROM gate_for_ea_base WHERE source_name IN ('ea_request') AND row_count > 0 HAVING count(*) = 1) gate
WHERE rn = 1
transformation_flows.source_description: UC6 silver: the EA base file -- one row per osapr, carrying its targetAreaID. The legacy design dedupes the request feed on {osapr}; ROW_NUMBER over the ingestion timestamp makes 'which duplicate wins' explicit and deterministic rather than arbitrary.

transformation_flows.transformation_sql:
WITH ea AS (
  SELECT trim(osapr) AS osapr, targetAreaID, postcode,
         concat_ws(' ', sub_bld_name, bld_name, bld_number, thfare2, thfare1, dbl_dep_loc, dep_loc) AS address_raw,
         town AS town_raw, po_box
  FROM ea_request_for_address
  WHERE osapr IS NOT NULL AND trim(osapr) <> ''
), normalised AS (
  SELECT osapr, targetAreaID,
         nullif(upper(regexp_replace(coalesce(postcode, ''), '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '')), '') AS postcode_norm,
         nullif(trim(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(upper(coalesce(address_raw, '')), '[^A-Z0-9 ]', ' '), ' +', ' ')), '') AS address_norm,
         nullif(trim(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(upper(coalesce(town_raw, '')), '[^A-Z0-9 ]', ' '), ' +', ' ')), '') AS town_norm,
         po_box IS NOT NULL AND trim(po_box) <> '' AS has_po_box
  FROM ea
), deduped AS (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY postcode_norm, address_norm, town_norm ORDER BY osapr) AS rn
  FROM normalised
)
SELECT osapr, postcode_norm, address_norm, town_norm, has_po_box, targetAreaID
FROM deduped
CROSS JOIN (SELECT count(*) AS present_sources FROM gate_for_ea_address WHERE source_name IN ('ea_request') AND row_count > 0 HAVING count(*) = 1) gate
WHERE rn = 1
transformation_flows.source_description: UC6 silver: the normalised EA address set -- deduped on {postcode, address, town} per the legacy design, carrying osapr for the join back to the base file. PO Box rows are retained here and excluded at match time, so the exclusion is visible in one place rather than implied by absence.

transformation_flows.transformation_sql:
WITH css AS (
  SELECT s.msisdn, a.postcode,
         concat_ws(' ', a.building_name1, a.building_name, a.building_number, a.street1, a.street2, a.locality1, a.locality2) AS address_raw,
         a.county AS town_raw, a.po_box
  FROM css_subscription_in s
  JOIN css_account_in c ON s.customerid = c.customerid
  JOIN css_account_address_in a ON c.customerid = a.customerid
  WHERE c.customerbusinessunitcode <> ${excluded_business_unit_code}
    AND c.dateofbirth IS NOT NULL
    AND floor((months_between(current_date, to_date(c.dateofbirth))) / 12) > ${min_age_years}
), jt AS (
  SELECT msisdn, postcode,
         concat_ws(' ', building_number, street2, locality2) AS address_raw,
         town AS town_raw, CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS po_box
  FROM jt_customer_in
  WHERE dateofbirth IS NOT NULL
    AND floor((months_between(current_date, to_date(dateofbirth, 'yyyyMMdd'))) / 12) > ${min_age_years}
), excalibur AS (
  SELECT msisdn, adr_post_code AS postcode,
         concat_ws(' ', adr_house_name,
                   coalesce(nullif(trim(regexp_replace(upper(concat_ws(' ', adr_house_no, adr_primary_ln)), '[^A-Z0-9 ]', ' ')), ''), adr_addr_line1),
                   adr_district) AS address_raw,
         adr_district AS town_raw, CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS po_box
  FROM excalibur_address_in
), customers AS (
  SELECT 'css' AS source_system, * FROM css
  UNION ALL SELECT 'jt', * FROM jt
  UNION ALL SELECT 'excalibur', * FROM excalibur
)
SELECT source_system, msisdn,
       nullif(upper(regexp_replace(coalesce(postcode, ''), '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '')), '') AS postcode_norm,
       nullif(trim(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(upper(coalesce(address_raw, '')), '[^A-Z0-9 ]', ' '), ' +', ' ')), '') AS address_norm,
       nullif(trim(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(upper(coalesce(town_raw, '')), '[^A-Z0-9 ]', ' '), ' +', ' ')), '') AS town_norm,
       po_box IS NOT NULL AND trim(po_box) <> '' AS has_po_box
FROM customers
CROSS JOIN (SELECT count(*) AS present_sources FROM gate_for_ee_paf WHERE source_name IN ('css_account', 'css_account_address', 'css_subscription', 'jt_customer', 'excalibur_address') AND row_count > 0 HAVING count(*) = 5) gate
WHERE msisdn IS NOT NULL AND trim(msisdn) <> ''
transformation_flows.source_description: UC6 silver: every EE address normalised into the common PAF shape and unioned -- CSS (PAYM/OUK, the three-way join plus the age>17 and unit-code<>'BS' business filters), JT (PAYG/OUK) and Excalibur (EE/TMUK). One flow with a UNION ALL rather than three staging tables, per the repo's Single-Read DAG mandate rule 3: reshaping before a union belongs inside the consuming table. Excalibur's two record variants are reconciled with a coalesce rather than a separate branch.

transformation_flows.transformation_sql: SELECT ea.osapr, ea.targetAreaID, ea.postcode_norm AS postcode, ea.address_norm AS address, ea.town_norm AS town, ee.msisdn AS msisdn, ee.source_system, CASE WHEN ea.address_norm IS NULL OR ee.address_norm IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE cast(round(100.0 * size(array_intersect(split(ea.address_norm, ' '), split(ee.address_norm, ' '))) / greatest(size(split(ea.address_norm, ' ')), 1)) AS INT) END AS match_strength FROM ee_paf_in ee INNER JOIN ea_address_in ea ON ee.postcode_norm = ea.postcode_norm WHERE ea.has_po_box = false AND ee.has_po_box = false
transformation_flows.source_description: UC6 silver: EA addresses matched to EE addresses on normalised postcode, excluding PO Boxes, scored by address-token overlap. IMPORTANT: match_strength is a DOCUMENTED ASSUMPTION -- the legacy Ab Initio scoring algorithm appears in none of the supplied documents. It is deliberately confined to this one expression, and the threshold is a pipeline parameter, so it can be replaced wholesale when the real algorithm surfaces. See docs/UC6/BUILD_CONTRACT.md section 6.

transformation_flows.transformation_sql: WITH scored AS (  SELECT b.targetAreaID, b.osapr, max(coalesce(m.match_strength, 0)) AS best_match_strength,          count(DISTINCT m.msisdn) AS count_of_msisdn   FROM ea_base_in b LEFT JOIN matched_for_osapr m ON b.osapr = m.osapr   GROUP BY b.targetAreaID, b.osapr), area AS (  SELECT targetAreaID,          count(*) AS candidate_osapr_count,          sum(CASE WHEN best_match_strength > ${match_strength_threshold} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matched_osapr_count   FROM scored GROUP BY targetAreaID) SELECT s.targetAreaID, s.osapr,   CASE WHEN s.best_match_strength > ${match_strength_threshold}             AND a.matched_osapr_count > ${min_addresses_per_area} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS count,   CASE WHEN a.candidate_osapr_count <= ${min_addresses_per_area} THEN 'Single Addr'        WHEN s.best_match_strength <= ${match_strength_threshold} THEN 'Bad OSAPR'        WHEN a.matched_osapr_count > ${min_addresses_per_area} THEN 'Found'        ELSE 'Not Found' END AS status,   s.count_of_msisdn, a.matched_osapr_count AS count_of_osapr, s.best_match_strength AS match_strength FROM scored s JOIN area a ON s.targetAreaID = a.targetAreaID
transformation_flows.source_description: UC6 gold: one row per (targetAreaID, osapr) with its match COUNT and STATUS. Implements the four documented branches: Found (above threshold and the area has >1 matched address), Not Found (above threshold but only one), Bad OSAPR (at or below threshold), Single Addr (the area only ever had one address candidate at all). Both thresholds are pipeline parameters, never literals.

transformation_flows.transformation_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT m.targetAreaID, m.msisdn AS telephone
FROM matched_for_telephone m
JOIN osapr_for_telephone o ON m.targetAreaID = o.targetAreaID AND m.osapr = o.osapr
WHERE o.count = 1
  AND m.match_strength > ${match_strength_threshold}
transformation_flows.source_description: UC6 gold: the telephone list. Case 1 of the design (above threshold, MSISDN populated, and the area has more than one matched address) is included; Case 2 (only one matched address in the area) is EXCLUDED -- an anti-singling-out privacy safeguard, not an optimisation, so it is expressed as an explicit join against the areas that qualify rather than as a filter that could be lost in a rewrite.
UC6 egress 1 of 4: the Leidos telephone list, plain gzip (no GPG). Fields exactly targetAreaID|telephone, per the interface specification.

transformation_flows.transformation_sql: SELECT targetAreaID, osapr, count, status FROM osapr_for_leidos
transformation_flows.source_description: UC6 egress 2 of 4: the Leidos OSAPR match-status list, plain gzip (no GPG). Fields exactly targetAreaID|osapr|count|status.

UC6 egress 3 of 4: the Fujitsu-equivalent telephone list, gzip + GPG symmetric (AES256) under the br_digital_poc.config.pgpkey secret -- the same passphrase that decrypts the inbound EA request. Identical content to the Leidos file; the two exist so the Fujitsu-to-Leidos cutover can run in parallel with no gap in flood warnings.

transformation_flows.transformation_sql: SELECT targetAreaID, osapr, count, status FROM osapr_for_fujitsu
transformation_flows.source_description: UC6 egress 4 of 4: the Fujitsu-equivalent OSAPR match-status list, gzip + GPG symmetric.
